security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI configures a PMP entry with read permission (PMP_R) granting an S-mode domain shared read access to a memory region also accessed by M-mode firmware. The S-mode domain issues cbo.inval or cbo.flush on addresses within this region, evicting M-mode's cached entries (including potentially dirty cache lines of lock variables, IPC metadata, or domain state). M-mode subsequently reads stale memory or loses pending writes, violating the invariant that S-mode read-only access cannot perturb M-mode's view of shared memory.
security_spec.summary: CBO invalidation from S-mode on PMP_R shared regions can evict M-mode cached data, breaking firmware invariant that read-only S-mode access cannot perturb M-mode cache state

findings.finding: Unconditionally delegates cbo.inval and cbo.flush to S-mode hardware with ENVCFG_CBIE_INV (the most aggressive setting: invalidate without flush). With CBIE=INV, cbo.inval silently evicts cache lines without first writing back dirty data, even on read-only memory. M-mode's dirty cache lines in shared SUR_MRW/SUR_MR regions are vulnerable to silent eviction by a malicious S-mode domain.

Domain memory access check has no concept of CBO operations. The access_flags only recognizes SBI_DOMAIN_READ, WRITE, EXECUTE, MMIO. A cbo.inval issued by S-mode on a SUR_MRW/SUR_MR region passes the check as a 'read', even though cbo.inval is a destructive cache eviction, not a data load. No SBI_DOMAIN_CBO_INVAL or SBI_DOMAIN_CBO_FLUSH access type exists to distinguish cache operations from true reads.

SUR_MRW regions (SU read-only, M read/write) are encoded as PMP_W under Smepmp. This PMP encoding grants S-mode read access but cannot distinguish between a data load and a cache eviction (cbo.inval). The PMP hardware has no mechanism to block cache-block operations independently of reads. For SUR_MR regions, the encoding is PMP_L|PMP_R|PMP_W|PMP_X (line 164), which similarly grants read access allowing cbo.inval.

Domain context switch saves/restores S-mode CSRs (sstatus, sie, stvec, sscratch, sepc, scause, stval, sip, satp, scounteren, senvcfg) but never reads, modifies, or restores menvcfg. The CBIE=INV and CBCFE=1 settings persist unchanged across domain boundaries. If one domain should be restricted from CBO operations on shared memory, menvcfg must be adjusted per-domain.

When M-mode yields to S-mode, this function sets mstatus.MPP, mepc, stvec/sscratch/sie/satp but never modifies menvcfg. The CBIE=INV and CBCFE=1 bits set by mstatus_init() remain active from the first instruction executed in S-mode. There is no window where CBO delegation is downgraded (e.g., to CBIE_FLUSH to force dirty writeback before eviction) before handing control to less-privileged code.

The default trap case unconditionally redirects unrecognized traps to S-mode. Since CBO instructions are fully delegated via menvcfg (CBCFE=1, CBIE=INV), they never trap to M-mode, so this code path is not reached for CBO. No vulnerability here, but it also means there's no last-resort interception point if menvcfg delegation were to be restricted.

The access mask is 0x3f (6 bits: M_R/W/X and SU_R/W/X). Bits 6 and above are available but no CBO-related access flags are defined. The SUR_MR and SUR_MRW shared region types (lines 56-58, 75-78) grant SU_READABLE without any qualifier for cache-block operations. There is no SBI_DOMAIN_MEMREGION_NO_CBO flag to mark regions where cache-block operations from S-mode should be forbidden, and no SBI_DOMAIN_MEMREGION_CBO_ALLOWED bit to selectively permit them.
